segments.title: How Did the Exam Go?
segments.content:
June 15th, 3 p.m.

Zhang Wei, the head teacher of Class Five, Grade Nine at Yucai Middle School, was currently standing under the shade of a tree by the school gate to cool off.

Next to him was the head teacher of Class Six, Teacher Wang.

"Your year's class can be considered a great success," Teacher Wang said with a hint of envy, leaning against a tree branch. "A regular class produced two students admitted through independent recruitment, and one of them is the grade's perennial top student."

"Among the remaining students, there should be two or three more who are Fuyi High School material, right?"

"That kid Shao Heqi is definitely one, and then there's Xu Yinghuan, hmm... Jin Yuting has a good shot too."

"You, my friend, are infuriating."

After counting them out, Teacher Wang became even more envious.

You see.

Each grade at Yucai Middle School had two honors classes, while the other ten were regular classes. The student resources were worlds apart.

Normally, aside from a few individual students who couldn't keep up in the high-pressure environment, the honors classes basically swept the top hundred spots in exam rankings.

As for the students in regular classes, it was already quite good if two or three from each class could break into the top hundred.

Among them, it was even rarer for a regular class student to enter the top thirty of the entire school, as those spots were basically dominated by students from the honors classes.

However.

In their grade, a prodigy like Ying Chanxi had emerged.

From a regular class, she had effortlessly toppled the students from the honors classes, long occupying the throne of first in the grade, and finally, she had secured an independent recruitment spot with the greatest of ease.

If it were just that, it would be one thing.

But aside from Ying Chanxi, Zhang Wei's Class Five also had Zhao Rongjun, who was consistently in the top thirty, and Shao Heqi, in the top fifty.

Moreover, the class academic representative, Xu Yinghuan, and the English class representative, Jin Yuting, were also regulars in the school's top hundred.

For the head teacher of a regular class, such teaching achievements could be described as a glorious victory.

But Zhang Wei still shook his head modestly, "Let's not get ahead of ourselves. I'm not worried about Shao Heqi, but Xu Yinghuan and Jin Yuting tend to fluctuate quite a bit. Nothing is certain until the results are out."

After discussing the students who gave them peace of mind, the two teachers moved on to others, including Li Luo.

"It's those kids like Li Luo who are the most worrisome," Zhang Wei sighed. "Stuck hovering right around the cutoff for regular high school, I have no idea if they can make it."

As teachers, they naturally hoped their students' scores would be as high as possible.

Especially for students like Li Luo, who were just a little short of getting into a regular high school, the teachers all hoped they could perform exceptionally well on the high school entrance exam.

After all, it was also tied to their own teaching performance, which was linked to school bonuses and professional titles.

The better the class's overall performance, the more benefits there were for the head teacher.

Just then, the bell signaling the end of the final English exam rang.

A few minutes later, the students walked out of the examination hall with various expressions on their faces.

Some were full of confidence, some were a mix of joy and worry, and others were covered in a gloomy haze.

"How did the exam go?" Ying Chanxi asked as soon as she met up with Li Luo at the school gate.

"When I'm on the case, you can rest easy," Li Luo said, patting his chest in assurance.

Hearing him say this, Ying Chanxi squinted at him, "You usually can't even pass English. How am I supposed to rest easy?"

"Last night, you opened up my Ren and Du meridians. When I looked at the English exam paper today, I actually recognized every single word."

"You're full of nonsense. I don't want to talk to you anymore."

"Why does no one believe the truth these days?"

The two of them walked toward Li Guohong by the roadside, bickering all the way.

On their way, Shao Heqi and Jin Yuting, who had just come out of the examination hall, walked over.

"Li Luo, how did the exam go?" Shao Heqi greeted him first, asking with a smile, "This time's English paper was quite simple. You might have been able to pass."

"She helped me review yesterday." Li Luo pointed at Ying Chanxi beside him. "I feel like I can score over a hundred this time."

"Are you dreaming?" Jin Yuting, who had still been upset about her poor performance on the morning's science exam, couldn't help but raise her eyebrows and mock Li Luo upon hearing his words. "This English paper looked simple, but the reading comprehension questions had quite a few little traps. I think you'll have a hard time even passing."

Li Luo didn't care about Jin Yuting's taunts. He just smiled without responding and said to Ying Chanxi, "Let's go, my dad's waiting."

"Okay." Ying Chanxi nodded and waved to her two classmates. "Bye, we're heading back now."

"Hey, wait!" Shao Heqi remembered something and quickly called out to them. "I'm planning to talk to Teacher Zhang about having a class gathering for Class Five after the results come out. What do you think, class president?"

"That," Ying Chanxi paused and thought for a moment. "The students admitted to Fuyi High School through independent recruitment have to attend the early summer session in a few days, so it would be best to set the time for a weekend."

"I'll have to be at Fuyi High for class then, so I might have to trouble you with arranging this."

"Or if you run into any problems, you can also ask Li Luo for help."

"No problem, no problem at all!" The moment Shao Heqi heard Ying Chanxi entrusting him with this, he patted his chest vigorously and loudly guaranteed, "No need for Li Luo, I'll arrange it well with Teacher Zhang."

"I'll leave it to you then," Ying Chanxi said politely. "If there's nothing else, we'll head home."

After talking with Shao Heqi and the others, Li Luo and Ying Chanxi continued walking toward Li Guohong by the side of the road.

At this moment, Li Guohong was in the middle of a lively chat with Li Luo's maternal uncle, Wei Dongrong.

When he saw Li Luo walk over, Li Guohong said to the other man, "I'll find some time to go take a look in a couple of days then."

"No problem, you're welcome anytime." Wei Dongrong laughed heartily. "We can have a meal together then, and I'll give you a proper introduction."

After the two sides said their goodbyes, Li Guohong led the two kids home.

Lin Xiuhong didn't come.

Mainly because she didn't want to get angry at Zhang Xuefen, so she went straight to the wet market to buy groceries instead.

Following behind Li Guohong, Li Luo turned his head to look not far away, where his cousin Wei Chun was getting into a red Audi, and Wei Dongrong's back disappeared into the front passenger seat. He couldn't help but fall into deep thought.

He glanced at his own father and sighed softly.

In his previous life, because of his rebellious phase, Li Guohong hadn't closed the breakfast shop during his entrance exams and had never come to pick him up at the school gate.

So, in his last life, it was probably a month or two later that his uncle Wei Dongrong had sought out Li Guohong to recommend the investment.

But after being reborn, due to a twist of fate, this matter had been moved up.

From the looks of it, if Li Guohong went to see that real estate project in a couple of days and was persuaded by Wei Dongrong, he might invest the first sum of money very soon.

Once his parents got a taste of the first short-term profit, whatever Li Luo, this little kid, said would be useless.

At this thought, Li Luo frowned, feeling rather helpless.

Returning to the age of 15, he felt a certain degree of awkwardness when facing some situations, unable to handle them with the identity of an adult.

"How did the exam go?" Li Guohong glanced at his son. Having snapped out of his earlier conversation, he was now concerned about the boy's results.

"Not bad."

"Compared to the mock exams?"

"Definitely better than the mock exams."

"Any chance for a regular high school?"

"Definitely a chance!"

Looking at Li Luo's confident face, Li Guohong was actually a bit unsure, so he looked at Ying Chanxi next to him, "Xixi, what do you think?"

"It should... be fine, right?" Ying Chanxi wasn't sure either. After all, it was Li Luo who took the exam, not her.

Although Li Luo had been exceptionally serious while reviewing these past two days, Ying Chanxi didn't know if it had actually helped or improved anything.

So she added, "Why don't we wait for the exam content to be released in a couple of days, and I can help him check his answers?"

"Why go to all that trouble." Li Luo shook his head and said, "The results will be out at the end of the month anyway, we can just see then."

"That's true." Li Guohong thought about it and decided not to dwell on it. "It's all set in stone after the exam. A few more days won't make a difference."

Back at home.

Ying Chanxi naturally followed them into Li Luo's house and ran to the kitchen to help Lin Xiuhong prepare the food.

It was only three-thirty in the afternoon, still early for dinner.

But to celebrate the successful conclusion of Li Luo's high school entrance exam, Lin Xiuhong had bought a huge amount of groceries and planned to cook something nice, so she had started preparing now.

"Look at Xixi, and then look at you," Lin Xiuhong said to Li Luo in the living room. "You've got nothing to do now that your exams are over, right? Come in and help."

That's how students were.

Before exams, they were precious treasures. After exams, they were free labor.

Li Luo obediently walked into the kitchen, received the task of peeling garlic from his dear mother, and squatted by the trash can, working diligently.

"How did your exam go?" Lin Xiuhong asked while prepping the vegetables.

"Mom, you're already the fourth person to ask me," Li Luo sighed and said, "Repeating the same thing over and over feels like a waste of life."

"Why is your mouth so sharp?" Lin Xiuhong glared at him. "By your logic, me cooking for you every day is also a waste of life, right?"

"How could that be?" Li Luo shook his head repeatedly. "According to data from the Women's Federation, a housewife's annual domestic labor is valued at 1.24 million, which is more than three thousand a day."

"Just this one meal of yours must be worth at least a few hundred."

"Mom, you're creating value for society, quietly contributing. You're great and selfless."

"Just shut up," Lin Xiuhong scoffed. "If there really was that much money, wouldn't I be better off being a nanny for someone else? Who's going to pay me an annual salary of 1.24 million? I'd even take 240,000."

"Ask Dad to pay you," Li Luo blinked and gestured toward the living room with his chin.

But Li Guohong in the living room had ears sharper than a dog's and immediately laughed and scolded, "You little brat, I don't even have any secret stash of cash, so don't you run your mouth!"

"Don't change the subject," Lin Xiuhong realized and continued to ask, "So how did the exam really go?"

"Alright, I'll be direct," Li Luo sighed. "Mom, you'd better get ready to buy me a new phone."

"What do you mean?"

"Didn't you say it yesterday? If I get into Fuyi High School, you'll buy me a phone."

"...Xixi."

"What is it, Auntie Lin?"

"Shove that cucumber of yours in his mouth. He's so annoying."

"Oh."

"Wait... holy crap, you're really doing it? You haven't even scraped off the thorns!"
